title: Elsham Wolds — Black Swan Memorial (Halifax JD386)
crew_summary: 7 killed including pilot Plt Off. Johann Sigurdson

crew.name: Johann Sigurdson
crew.burial_location: Harrogate (Stonefall) Cemetery, Sec F, Row C, Grave 3
crew.bio: Son of Sigurthor and Maria Osk Sigurdson, husband of Mary Eileen Sigurdson, of Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. The only Icelandic-born bomber pilot killed in WW2. Sigurdson Peninsula in Manitoba was named in his honour in 1995.

crew.name: Robert Thomas Garth Loughrin
crew.burial_location: Harrogate (Stonefall) Cemetery, Sec F, Row B, Grave 17
crew.bio: Son of Joseph G. Loughrin and Maude E. Loughrin, of Cookstown, Co. Tyrone, Northern Ireland. Grave inscription: "Safe In The Arms Of Jesus".

crew.name: George Lindley Muskett
crew.burial_location: Harrogate (Stonefall) Cemetery, Sec F, Row B, Grave 20
crew.bio: Son of Henry Joseph Salisbury Muskett and Winifred Janet Muskett, husband of Joan Elizabeth Muskett, of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

crew.name: John Burgess Eaton
crew.burial_location: Harrogate (Stonefall) Cemetery, Sec F, Row B, Grave 19
crew.bio: Son of Charles Edward and Margaret Lydia Eaton, of Oshawa, Ontario, Canada. Grave inscription: "Till The Sunshine Of To-Morrow Lifts The Shadows Of To-Day".

crew.name: Joseph M. Healey
crew.burial_location: Harrogate (Stonefall) Cemetery, Sec F, Row C, Grave 2
crew.bio: Son of Thomas R. Healey and Catherine Healey, of the USA. Grave inscription: "Jesus Have Mercy On Him Mary And Joseph Pray For Him".

crew.name: Francis Elvin Wilt
crew.burial_location: Harrogate (Stonefall) Cemetery, Sec F, Row B, Grave 18
crew.bio: Son of Elvin Edward and Selena Mabel Wilt, of Stelcam, Saskatchewan, Canada. Wilt Lake in Saskatchewan was named in his honour. Grave inscription: "Among Honored Comrades Our Son 'Rest On Thy Duty Done' From His Home In Canada".

crew.name: Peter Zayets
crew.burial_location: Harrogate (Stonefall) Cemetery, Sec F, Row C, Grave 1
crew.bio: Son of Alexander and Maria Zayets, of Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. Zayets Lake was named in his honour in 1974. His brother, Sgt Stephen Zayets (R/56703 RCAF), was also killed — on 14 July 1943 with 428 Squadron, buried in Florennes Communal Cemetery, Belgium. Grave inscription: "In Loving Memory Of Our Dear Son And Brother Peter".

memorial_address: RAF Elsham Wolds Memorial Rooms and Garden, Middle Gate Lane, Elsham, DN20 0PH
memorial_access_notes: Located on the old airfield site, now owned by Anglian Water. Protected by a high fenced compound with controlled access gate. The memorial is inside the compound, maintained by volunteers of the RAF Elsham Wolds Memorial Rooms and Garden.

external_narratives.summary: Comprehensive page on P/O Johann Sigurdson and crew of Halifax JD386. All seven crew (six RCAF, one RAFVR) were killed when the aircraft crashed near Wressle on 29 February 1944. They were buried with full military honours at Harrogate Cemetery on 8 March 1944.
external_narratives.key_details: Sigurdson was the only Icelandic bomber pilot killed in WW2. Sigurdson Peninsula in Manitoba was named in his honour in 1995. His wife was Mary Eileen Sigurdson of Winnipeg. This was the first major accident from 1666 HCU since June 1943.
external_narratives.link_description: Detailed information about P/O Johann Sigurdson and Halifax JD386 crew's tragic crash site at Elsham Wolds Memorial.

external_narratives.summary: Entry from the RAF Elsham Wolds memorial database documenting the loss of Halifax JD386 from 1666 HCU RAF Wombleton. Aircraft crashed at Bridge Farm, Broughton at 17:10 hours during a training flight.
external_narratives.key_details: Aircraft crashed at Bridge Farm, Broughton. Unit was 1666 HCU based at RAF Wombleton, not Elsham Wolds itself. Crash time recorded as 17:10 hours.

narrative: Flying from their station at Elsham Wolds, the crew of Halifax JD386 were undertaking a training sortie with 1666 Heavy Conversion Unit when the aircraft crashed on 29 February 1944. Pilot Officer Johann Sigurdson commanded a crew of seven drawn from Canada, Britain, and the United States. The Halifax came down at Elsham Wolds in Lincolnshire, and there were no survivors. All seven men were killed, among them Flight Engineer Sergeant Robert Thomas Garth Loughrin, who was just 20 years old.
